about: MUTATING — grow ONE instance's PersistentVolumeClaim on Longhorn (infra/forge/expand-instance-volume.sh <namespace> <pvc> <size> <plan_sha256>) through the forge's ops_kubectl door (the admin kubeconfig David placed, infra/estate/ops-credentials.sh). Asked for by David 2026-10-01 (backlog ebbb923f, incident d3c0a67c): the system of record's database volume boss/pgdata-postgres-0 filled, and its first expansion was his hand kubectl patch, which must be the last — and his first try, 20Gi -> 40Gi, was REFUSED by Longhorn's admission webhook because one replica's ~110 GiB disk had ~10.7 GiB of scheduling room. AUTHORISED PER RUN BY DAVID'S PASSKEY in design 17835005's shape, as set-volume-replicas and commission-a-disk are: it declares requires_approval with the read-only plan-an-instance-volume-expansion (this script's --plan) as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey on the approvers list signs those bytes, and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan; the script re-renders and patches nothing unless today's plan hashes to it. The size before is in the bytes, so a second run of an applied plan is refused: at most once. THE BOUND IS THE SCRIPT'S, NEVER A PARAM: the namespace is one of infra/cluster/instances.toml's (derived through render-instance.sh --instances; boss-dev and every system namespace refused); the claim exists, is Bound, has no expansion in flight; its StorageClass is driver.longhorn.io with allowVolumeExpansion true; the Longhorn volume behind it is this claim's, its spec.size is the claim's capacity, its robustness healthy; the size is whole GiB, larger than now (grows only), at most 2x per run and at most the script's CEILING_GIB (100); and for EVERY disk holding a replica, both halves of Longhorn v1.11.3's CheckReplicasSizeExpansion with required = replicas-on-the-disk x growth — ValidateDiskAvailableForExpansion on the disk's physical space (physicalUsed = storageMaximum - storageAvailable - storageReserved; physicalUsed + required <= (storageMaximum - storageReserved) x storage-over-provisioning-percentage / 100, and storageMaximum - (physicalUsed + required) at or above the storage-minimal-available-percentage floor), then IsSchedulableToDisk on the ledger (storageScheduled + required <= that same limit, storageAvailable above the floor); the physical half was added after adversarial review adc832e2 found a growth the ledger admitted and the disk could not hold — so a size the webhook would refuse is refused before any write, naming the largest size that fits. THE WRITE is one kubectl patch pvc --type=json that TESTS spec.resources.requests.storage is still the planned value and replaces it — a compare-and-set on the one field. THE EFFECT IS READ BACK: every 10 s for up to 600 s, the claim's status.capacity.storage and the Longhorn volume's spec.size; only when both read the new size in bytes is the effect line printed, and otherwise the run exits 1 saying the claim is NOT proven, naming the capacity, the request, the claim's conditions (FileSystemResizePending is the kubelet's half) and Longhorn's spec.size. Timeout 900, inside which the script's own 600 s read-back gives its verdict before the runner's kill.
effect: ^expand-instance-volume: [a-z0-9-]+/[a-z0-9-]+ is [0-9]+Gi — read back: status\.capacity\.storage [^ ]+ \([0-9]+ bytes\), Longhorn volume [0-9a-z-]{40} spec\.size [0-9]+, robustness [a-z]+ \(after [0-9]+s\)$
